newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party sets poll for chief in July.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party sets poll for chief in July.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Friday that it would hold organisational elections next month, leading to the election of a party president in July.

The party, responding to an order from the Election Commission directing leading parties to hold organisational elections, said in a statement that it would hold cadre elections between June 6 and June 19 across the country.

These elections would lead to the choosing of district and block, or sub-district level, delegates who will form a nationwide electoral college of 6,500 delegates to choose a national president for the party, Congress officials said.
The delegates are scheduled to vote on July 11, if a contest were found necessary, to elect the Congress president, the statement said.
The current Congress president, Sitaram Kesri, was chosen last September by the Congress Working Committee (CWC) after the resignation of his predecessor, former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The CWC is elected by the party's general body, the All India Congress Committee (AICC). A new AICC is scheduled to be elected by nationwide cadres on July 12, Congress officials said.

Kesri's election had to be ratified by a plenary meeting of the AICC, but this was now considered unnecessary as fresh elections were being held to choose a president, Congress leader Pranab Mukherjee told a news conference.

Congress, which has ruled India for all but five years since independence from Britain in 1947, suffered its worst electoral humiliation last year, but still holds clout through its make-or-break support for the ruling coalition.

Kesri plunged the United Front into a crisis in March by withdrawing his party's support, leading to the defeat of prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition in a parliamentary confidence vote on April 11.
The alliance then chose Inder Kumar Gujral as the new prime minister to win back Congress' support.
